assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational physiological discovery translated into a major therapeutic class with exceptional benefit in diabetes and obesity.
assessment.attribution: Holst, Mojsov, and Drucker represent key discovery and physiological-developmental contributions, although the broader translational history is extensive.
assessment.maturity: The biology and therapeutic effects have been confirmed over decades across large clinical populations.
uncertainties: The candidate description encompasses both fundamental physiology and drug development, making the three-person allocation necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing provided a decisive molecular therapy for a previously devastating inherited neuromuscular disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer and Bennett provide a compact and credible pairing of mechanistic splicing insight and therapeutic antisense development.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy and durable real-world impact support a mature recognition.
uncertainties: The relative contributions of additional academic and clinical-development participants are not specified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Modern cochlear implants transformed profound deafness from a largely irreversible sensory deficit into recoverable speech perception for many recipients.
assessment.attribution: Clark, Hochmair, and Wilson plausibly cover the essential implant and speech-processing advances.
assessment.maturity: The intervention has longstanding, replicated clinical utility and broad global impact.
uncertainties: The contribution was a cumulative engineering and clinical enterprise, so priority boundaries may be difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CAR-T cells established a new therapeutic principle: genetically redirecting living immune cells to treat cancer.
assessment.attribution: Rosenberg, Sadelain, and June form a strong three-person account of the conceptual, engineering, and clinical translation.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved therapies and durable responses establish clinical maturity, particularly in hematologic malignancies.
uncertainties: Effectiveness, toxicity, access, and extension to solid tumors remain uneven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING revealed a central mechanism by which cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune signaling, reshaping understanding of infection, autoimmunity, and cancer immunity.
assessment.attribution: Chen, Ishikawa, and Sun are a focused proposed group for discovery and mechanistic definition, despite a wider relevant literature.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is deeply integrated into immunology and has broad experimental confirmation.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation has not yet matched the maturity of the fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 human genetics and biology delivered unusually direct validation of a cardiovascular therapeutic target with major public-health relevance.
assessment.attribution: Hobbs, Cohen, and Seidah represent complementary genetic and biological contributions, though the stated candidate group is larger.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is well established and therapeutic inhibition has demonstrated substantial LDL-cholesterol lowering and clinical benefit.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of recognition among genetic discovery, biochemical discovery, and drug development remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CFTR modulators turned mechanistic understanding of channel dysfunction into transformative precision treatments for cystic fibrosis.
assessment.attribution: Welsh, Van Goor, and Negulescu provide a plausible mechanism-to-therapeutic-development allocation.
assessment.maturity: Clinical benefits across eligible genotypes are well demonstrated and have changed disease prognosis.
uncertainties: The achievement depends on a long chain of prior CFTR discovery and broad industrial development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TNF blockade established a durable therapeutic principle for rheumatoid arthritis and several inflammatory diseases.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are a clear, appropriately bounded pair for the translational immunology underlying this advance.
assessment.maturity: Its efficacy, limitations, and broad clinical impact are established over decades.
uncertainties: The discovery is therapeutically transformative, while its fundamental mechanistic novelty relative to other leading candidates is harder to weigh.
